_coins: D253: every amount of money in data/ is copper (100 a silver, 100 silver a gold, 100 gold a platinum); see src/chronicle/coins.gd and docs/26.

tracks._comment: D233: dirt tracks between the places people live (src/area/tracks.gd). Each place is joined to its nearest `links` others no further than `reach` tiles; a signpost stands where `signpost_ways` or more ways leave open ground.

from_afar._comment: Who speaks from afar is seen as a ghost of themselves (play-test 7, doug-md: Sennet 'as a ghostly blue figure'; call BR8). A line sent with `afar` by a speaker named here shows their face in the talk box washed in `tint`, and on the ground their figure stands `beside` cells off the lead's shoulder in the same wash, coming in over `fade` seconds and flickering by `flicker`, gone when the talk is over. Read by src/dialogue/dialogue_script.gd and src/area/area_scene.gd.

climbers_stone._comment: The stone at the Tower's door with the names of those who climbed and how high each got (play-test 7, doug-md: 'names of climbers on the Tower', call BR3). Read by src/chronicle/climbers.gd: every lead fallen in the sixteen's worlds before this one (Sixteen.worlds), highest first, then this lead while they climb. `top` is the line over them all: **Inferred** (agenda 177), the legendary company of six who climbed long ago (call BR1), unnamed until doug-md names them.
climbers_stone.heading: Names are cut into the stone, one under another, each with how high they got.
climbers_stone.none: Under them, the stone is smooth and waiting.
climbers_stone.top: At the top, cut deeper and older than the rest, six names worn too smooth to read.

first_hour._comment: The First Hour's cut list (D95, D97): systems built but hidden until the First Hour plays from the crater to floor 5. Read by src/chronicle/first_hour.gd. Take a name out of `hidden` to bring its system back. coliseum: the Extras entry and the keep doors; training: the Extras entry (the suites still use it); museum: the Extras entry; trivia: no facts found; grimoires: no books for sale; ferries: no sailing; captivity: nobody is taken alive; nemesis: no foe remembers you (back since D330, call BX); dispatch: nobody is sent on errands from the party screen; seasons: no season on the bar, in the journal or the news; beds: no bed to buy in the crater, which is where the lead fell, not a home (D178); The roadside scenes (D121) came back once drawn and stood on the ground (D131).
first_hour._comment_guild_mark: D101: nobody climbs without the Guild's mark. With `guild_mark` on, every run starts with the Tower's stair sealed, the way a chapter's end seals it (src/chronicle/chapters.gd), and the first gate the company shuts opens it. `mark_line` is what the Tower's doorkeeper says while it is shut. **Inferred**: the mark is earned by shutting any gate, with or without the Guild's contract on it.
first_hour.mark_line: Nobody climbs without the Guild's mark. Sennet keeps the Guild's register: shut a gate and he marks you for the Tower.
first_hour._comment_first_life: D106: the first life is always this lead. New Game with no world yet ended starts here, skipping the quiz; the quiz picks the next lead after a death.
first_hour._comment_gate_after_city: AU (D161, the five strangers): after the city, before any gate is shut, the compass and Auto point at the nearest gate at the lead's rank (Greyhollow) instead of the Guild at the Tower's door, and Sennet says why the first time the party walks into a town. `gate_line` is his line; {gate} is the gate's name. Off, the compass sends the party to the Guild first (D107). Read by FirstHour.gate_after_city and world_scene._arrive_at.
first_hour.gate_line: New down, are you? Nobody climbs the Tower without the Guild's mark, and the mark is earned at a gate. {gate} is open and near. Shut it, then find me at the Tower's door.
first_hour._comment_deal_only_written: AQ (D145): while some of the sixteen have no chapter one in data/memories.json, the quiz deals only those who do, so a second life never climbs to an empty alcove. Read by FirstHour.unwritten_tempers. Once every lead has a chapter one it holds nobody back; take it out then.
first_hour._comment_light_out: AK (D149): the hour's end costs somebody. The first time the lead wins floor `floor`, one of the other sixteen falls in a world of their own (never the lead, the company, a lead already fallen, or one met at a crossing), picked by the world's seed; the census counts them out from then on. `lines` are what the Tower shows, {name} the one who fell. Read by FirstHour.put_out_a_light.

lines: High in the Tower's glass, sixteen small lights burn. As you stand there, one of them gutters, and goes out.
{name}. Somewhere, in a world of their own, {name} fell while you climbed.

first_hour._comment_warden: D184 (D174): the floor 5 keeper speaks once as its fight begins, and counts the challengers: which of the sixteen leads this is in the run of worlds, the first life the `first`, after that lead has died the next the second, up to the sixteenth (`last_line`). Leads fallen in earlier worlds are counted (Sixteen.fallen_heroes, kept outside the save, D47); climbers who are not leads never are. `band` is the keeper's band key, `speaker` who the box names, `ordinals` the words for first to sixteenth; `first_line` is the first life's, `line` every other's, {ordinal} the word and {name} the lead. Read by FirstHour.warden_line and area_scene._fight_held. The wording is **Inferred** (agenda 108).

warden.speaker: The Warden of the Fifth
warden.first_line: The first challenger arrives. {name}. I know your face, and the world you fell into.
warden.line: The {ordinal} challenger approaches. {name}. I know your face; I knew the ones before you.
warden.last_line: The sixteenth and final challenger approaches. {name}. There is nobody after you.

first_hour._comment_tenth_keeper: D254: the Keeper of the Tenth, at the top of the Second Hour, speaks once as its fight begins as the Warden does, and counts the same way. **Inferred**: every word.

tenth_keeper.speaker: The Keeper of the Tenth
tenth_keeper.first_line: Ten floors, {name}, and you remember two chapters of yourself. The Warden counted you first. So do I.
tenth_keeper.line: {name}. The {ordinal} to reach the tenth. The ones before you remembered as much, and it did not carry them up.
tenth_keeper.last_line: {name}. The sixteenth. When you are gone the stair has nobody left to keep it from.

first_hour._comment_auto_rest: D210 (call BL): a party walking itself whose health is under this share of its whole goes to the nearest place that heals it on arriving (a village, keep or hut; not the crater) before any band or the objective. Read by AutoRoad.rest_stop. **Inferred**: the share.
first_hour._comment_auto_climb: D258: a party walking itself goes up the Tower only with its health at auto_climb_above of its whole or more, resting first (AutoRoad.rest_stop), and turns back down a floor to rest when under auto_turn_back_below (area_scene._auto_axis); the floors it won stay won. Before, the bots climbed on hurt and fell on floors 1 to 4 in every run. **Inferred**: both shares.
first_hour._comment_auto_seeks_rest: D402 (found by bot play, 2026-10-23): knowing no village, keep or hut it can rest at by arriving (only the walled city it woke in, which is walked into, not rested at), a party walking itself makes for the nearest one there is, as if it took the road out to find one. Before, it had nowhere to rest, so it climbed the Tower at half health and fell on floor 2. **Inferred**: that Auto may head for a place it has not seen.
first_hour._comment_auto_hearthwick: D367 (found by the bot, 2026-10-22): in a place that goes back to the title when left (Atlas's Last Stand in Hearthwick, never saved), Auto does not walk: pressed, it says auto_hearthwick_line and stays off. Before, it walked the two cells to the road south and the tutorial ended at the title. **Inferred**: the words.
first_hour.auto_hearthwick_line: Auto walks the company on once you are out in the world. Here, walk Hearthwick yourself.
first_hour._comment_auto_hunt: D301: with levels only in gates, a party walking itself goes to the easiest gate standing instead of the Tower while the next floor's foes stand more than auto_hunt_gates_over levels above the company, or its keeper more than auto_hunt_keepers_over (AutoRoad.stair_too_hard). **Inferred**: both margins.
first_hour._comment_auto_stops: AM (D150): a party walking itself (Auto) stops for a fight that matters and hands it over paused: a gate's fight (`gates`), a keeper (`keepers`), or a foe more than `above_level` levels over the lead. It takes the walk back up once that fight is won. `line` is what the fight says when it stops. Since D300 a band of the land (a wild fight) never stops it: it is fought running and `ground_line` is said instead.

auto_stops.line: Auto stops here: this fight is yours.
auto_stops.ground_line: A hard one. Auto fights on: Q takes the party back.

life._comment: Life on the land (D179): birds, butterflies, bees, grasshoppers and snails, laid down a few to a tile and moving about; which picture does what is its `life` in props.json. per_tile: how many of each a tile of open country gets on average (a land's `life` in biomes.json scales it; a place gets half). art: the pictures each is drawn from. shy_cells: how close the party comes before a bird takes off; flee_cells [min, max]: how far it flies; flight_seconds and flight_height: the flight; away_seconds: how long one with nowhere to land stays gone. wander_flight: the chance, each time a bird has stood a while, that it goes up on a loop over the ground and comes down somewhere else, unscared (D189, play-test 4: "I want them flying around"); wander_cells [min, max] how far. road_watch: on the First Hour's road a pair of the city's Watch walks a tile of it in chance of the tiles, with these units, name, lines said at each end and talk.
life._comment_animals: A29, D370 (play-test 3: "Surely it would be some animals"): animals walking the land, per_tile on average to a tile of open country (a land's life scales it, a place gets half), each one of kinds (or a land's own life_art.animal in biomes.json), walking about roam_cells round where it was put. A kind walks only once its set is in at folder ({kind}: idle/<facing>.png, walk/<heading>/frame_000.png on); until then none is laid. names: what each is called; scale: its size against a person. Inferred: every number.
life._comment_climbers: D215 (play-test 4: "Other people trying to climb the tower." "I want to see more people in the environment."): other companies on their way up. On a road tile the Watch is not walking, at road_chance, a company of size[0] to size[1] walks the road there and back, the first of them saying one of lines at each end; on_the_floors, from floor `from` at `chance`, a company rests by the stair up. Their bodies are the four climber_ units, each drawn as the kin it was copied from until art row A33 lands in its art_wanted (D369), their name one of companies. They talk as any person (talk, on_the_floors.talk). A company within join_cells of a fight comes running and fights beside the party (D246), and a company on a floor sits round a fire of its own; with on_the_floors.join_anywhere a company resting on a floor joins a fight anywhere on that floor (play-test 7: floor 2's bands spot the party twelve cells from the stair). Inferred: every number, name and line.

climbers._comment_voices: Play-test 8, ask 2 (doug-md: the companies' talk was 'who are you, have you been up the Tower, any advice and goodbye' every time; call BX). Read by src/chronicle/company_talk.gd: each company in `companies` has its own voice here, its hello on the road, resting on a floor, or climbing a shared floor beside the party; its own answers to the three questions everyone asks (`who`, `up` on the road, `up_here` on a floor, `advice`), worded by the party from `wording`; two questions only it is asked (`own`); and its goodbye. `asks` are what else comes up where they are met, `place_asks` of them drawn the same way each time in the same place, each kept to floors `from` to `to`; `leave` is how the party takes its leave. `{floor}` and `{next}` are the floor met on and the one above. **Inferred** (agenda row on the companies' voices): every line here, for doug-md to mark.

hello: Copper Hands. If you're hiring, we cost more than we look. If you're not, we're walking the same way.
Mind your purse and we'll mind ours. Fair?
floor_hello: Sit if you like. The floor's free. Nothing else up here is.
Copper Hands, resting. Don't touch the packs.
shared_hello: Same floor as us, then. We fight, you fight, and nobody argues over the chests till after.
the Copper Hands.who: Five of us once, four now, paid by whoever pays. The Guild's mark is on our papers and the debts are on our backs.
the Copper Hands.up: To floor four, for a merchant who wanted a thing brought off it. He paid half. We're going back for the other half's worth.
the Copper Hands.up_here: Since the last fire burned down. We count in fires up here. Nobody keeps days on floor {floor}.
the Copper Hands.advice: Get paid before the stair, not after. And whatever drops, share it out on the spot. We've seen companies break over shares.

own.a: Silver was taken. Gold sounded like boasting. Copper is what we were worth when we started.
We work for coin, and you look short of it. Ask again when your purse weighs more than your sword.

the Copper Hands.bye: Coin's coin. Find us if you have some.
the Copper Hands.floor_bye: Don't die owing anyone. It follows you.

hello: Good day. We keep a lantern lit even at noon. An old habit, from inside.
You're for the Tower too? We'll trade maps, if you have any.
floor_hello: Quietly, please. We're drawing the floor.
Come into the light. Nothing up here likes it much.
shared_hello: We're mapping this floor as we go. Walk with us and you'll know where the walls are before you walk into them.
the Lantern Company.who: Mapmakers, mostly. The Guild buys our drawings of each floor, and the companies after us buy them from the Guild.
the Lantern Company.up: Floors one to six, drawn twice over. The second time we found a room the first map missed. We've been careful since.
the Lantern Company.up_here: Three lanterns' worth of oil. We count by oil. The map of floor {floor} is nearly done.
the Lantern Company.advice: Light every corner before you step into it. If a room seems bigger than the floor it sits on, write that down and go round.

own.a: This one isn't finished. Half a map is worse than none. It tells you where you're safe, and it's wrong.
Inside, the light goes wrong after a while. A flame you carry stays the colour it was. It tells you what's real.

the Lantern Company.floor_bye: Keep to the lit side. We've not drawn the dark corners yet.

hello: Ninth Stair.
You've a look about you. First climb?
floor_hello: Floor {floor}. We've seen worse. Not much worse.
shared_hello: Same floor, same stair. Keep up and we'll get along.
the Ninth Stair.who: We took our name from the ninth floor. Six of us reached it. Three came back down.
the Ninth Stair.up: Nine floors. Then we turned round. No shame in turning round.
the Ninth Stair.up_here: Long enough to stop counting. You don't get older in here, so the days don't add up to anything.
the Ninth Stair.advice: Never go up a stair tired. Never go up one angry. Never go up one alone.

own.q: What was on the ninth floor?
own.a: Ask me when I've had a drink. I'm not having one.
We left three of ours there. Somebody should go and see.

hello: Hob's Lot, that's us. Hob's the big one. The rest of us are his cousins, or say we are.
Hello there! Don't mind the smell of goat. We had a goat. Long story.
floor_hello: Pull up a bit of floor. Hob's doing the stew. It isn't the goat. Probably.
Another company! Hob, they've found us. Sit down, sit down.
shared_hello: Oh good, company! Hob says the more of us there are the louder we are, and the louder we are the fewer of them come.
Hob's Lot.who: Hob, his cousins, and his cousins' cousins. We had a farm out on the flats till a gate opened in the bottom field. So now we climb.
Hob's Lot.up: Floor two, for a bet. Floor three, by mistake. Hob wanted to see the top. We saw the next stair and that was plenty.
Hob's Lot.up_here: Since Hob's boots went through at the heel. A while, then.
Hob's Lot.advice: Eat first. Then fight. Then eat again. You'd be amazed how many lose for want of a dinner.

own.a: The big one. No, bigger. Him, by the pot.
Things came out of the gate and ate the sheep. The Guild shut it in the end. The sheep stayed eaten.

Hob's Lot.bye: Mind how you go! Hob says mind how you go.
Hob's Lot.floor_bye: Save us a bit of floor up there.

hello: We are the Grey Oath. We do not stop long.
Peace to you. We are going up, as you are.
floor_hello: Sit, if you wish. We keep a watch while we rest.
You have climbed well to reach floor {floor}. So have we.
shared_hello: We will fight beside you on this floor. Our oath does not forbid it.
the Grey Oath.who: We swore an oath at the Tower's door, over the names of those who did not come down. We climb until one of us stands where they fell.
the Grey Oath.up: Each of us has been as high as the stone says. None of us higher. That is why we go again.
the Grey Oath.up_here: We do not count it. The oath does not care how long it takes, and in here our bodies do not care either.
the Grey Oath.advice: Say the names of your people before you climb, while they can hear you say them.

own.a: Our own dead. They are not yours to carry, and we do not ask it of you.

own.q: What happens when you keep the oath?
own.a: We have not thought so far ahead. That is the honest answer.

hello: Saltmen, off the coast. We're a long way from the water and we'd thank you not to mention it.
Fair winds. There aren't any here, but fair winds.
floor_hello: Drop anchor a while. There's nothing to drop it into, mind.
Floor {floor}. Dry as a ship's biscuit and twice as stale.
shared_hello: Two crews, one floor. We've sailed with worse. Keep off our port side and we'll get on.
the Saltmen.who: Fishermen, the lot of us, till the nets came up empty three seasons running. The Guild was paying for climbers. Climbing's rigging without the ship.
the Saltmen.up: Up to five and back, like a long tide. Out, turn, in. We'll go further on the next one.
the Saltmen.up_here: Two watches, maybe three. Hard to tell without a sky.
the Saltmen.advice: Tie yourselves together on the stairs. A rope's saved more of us than a sword has.

own.a: Every step. You don't miss a thing like that less for being high up.
Same reason the sheep went inland, we think. Something came out of the water, and the fish had more sense than us.

the Saltmen.floor_bye: Mind the swell on the stair. There isn't one. Mind it anyway.

hello: Oh! Hello. Are we late? We're usually late.
Late Risers. We'd have been here sooner but there was breakfast.
floor_hello: Is it morning? It feels like morning. We're going up after a nap.
Hello! Have you any bread? We've run out. We always run out.
shared_hello: You're on this floor too? Somebody at the Guild must have mixed up the order again. Lucky you.
the Late Risers.who: We meant to sign with the Copper Hands, but we slept through the day they took names. So we made our own company. Better name, anyway.
the Late Risers.up: Floor one, twice, and the start of two. We'd have done more, but somebody always needs a sit down.
the Late Risers.up_here: Ages. Or an hour. You can't tell in here, and none of us has got a day older, so it hardly matters.
the Late Risers.advice: Don't rush. Everyone rushes, and half of them are names on the stone now. We'd sooner be late.

own.a: We're still alive, aren't we? That's more than half the ones who started out with us.

own.q: Do you ever get up early?

the Late Risers.floor_bye: Go on ahead. We'll catch you up. Probably.

up: Have you been up the Tower?
How far up have you been?
up_here: How long have you been up here?
How long have you been on this floor?
advice: What would you tell a company going up?

road.a: A gate open off to the side a day back. We gave it room. The Guild will have it marked by now.
The Tower, same as everyone on this road. There's nowhere else it goes.

road.q: Is the Guild's mark hard to get?
road.a: Shut a gate and it's yours. Shutting the gate is the hard part.
Enough that the road's busy. Not enough that the inns are full.
Loud, walled and dear. Everything you need, at twice what it's worth.

floor.a: The same as this one, only more of it, and it knows you're coming.

floor.q: Is floor five as bad as they say?
floor.a: Worse. Whatever keeps floor five has kept it a long time. Go up rested or don't go up.
The floors have ground of their own from here. As if the Tower stopped copying itself.

floor.q: Why do the floors keep growing?
floor.a: Nobody knows. Every floor's a room or two bigger than the one below, as if the Tower were still being built from the inside.
Rooms, more of them, and something in each. Clear them one at a time and rest between.

floor.q: Does anything come down the stair?
floor.a: Not while you sit by it. That's why everyone rests here.
Bits of them. Packs left on a stair. A cold fire. You learn not to look too closely.

floor.q: Have you heard of the six who went up long ago?
floor.a: They say the six are still alive, near floor seventy. Nobody ages in here. Whether they're still themselves is another question.

floor.q: Are there people living up here?
floor.a: Higher up, some floors have folk who stopped climbing and stayed. They'll rest you for coin. Fair enough, this high.

shared.q: Shall we take the rooms together?
shared.a: We'd planned on it. Clear a room, rest, then the next. We'll meet you at the stair.
Whoever's at the front. That's how it goes up here.

shared.q: Why are two companies on one floor?
shared.a: Every third floor or so the Tower lets two companies on at once. The Guild has a theory. Nobody believes it. We just say thank you.
Bigger rooms. Same as every floor up here. We'll know when we get there.

lines: Tower by nightfall, if your legs hold.
Don't stop. Stop and you think about it.
Floor three's where the last lot turned back.
Keep up. The Guild doesn't wait for anyone.

hello: Another one for the Tower? Good. The more of us go up, the fewer of them come down.
Walking the same way, are you? Everyone is, on this road.

ask.a: A company. Nobody you've heard of, yet. We've the Guild's mark and the better part of a map.

ask.q: Have you been up the Tower?
ask.a: Twice to floor two. Once to three. We came down quicker than we went up, but we came down.
Take the stair slow, eat when you can, and when something on a floor is bigger than the doorway it came through, leave it be.

hello: Easy. We're not what lives up here. Just resting our feet before the stair.
You made it this far, then. So did we, just.

ask.a: Couldn't tell you. Nobody who's been comes back down to say.
When my hands stop shaking. Go on ahead if you're in a hurry.

talk.bye: Mind the stair. It's steeper than it looks.

road_watch.name: a watchman of Stormreach
lines: Keep to the cobbles after dark.
Turn about. Back the way we came.

hello: The Watch keeps this road, from the crater to the Tower. Keep to it and you'll keep your purse.
Walk with us a stretch if you like. We don't go past the road's end.

ask.a: Safer than the grass either side of it. Bands come up off the open country; they don't like the cobbles, and they don't like us.
From where the fallen come down, through Stormreach, out to the first gate and back to the Tower. The Guild had it laid. Every new climber walks it.

road_watch._join_comment: D236 (doug-md, #270 keep 7, play-test 4: "The watchmen of anywhere. They will attack mobs"): lead a band to the Watch. When a band sets on the party within join_cells of a pair walking the road, they come running and fight beside it, at the company's level; won, they pay the Watch's bounty (purse_base + purse_per_level x the company's level) and the country hears of it (renown). Inferred: every number and line.
road_watch.joined_line: The Watch see it start, and come running.
thanks: "That's one band fewer on our road," says the older of them, getting his breath back.
"Bring us the next lot too. We'd sooner fight them here than find what they left."
road_watch.purse_line: He counts %s into your hand: the Watch's bounty on their heads.

auto_styles._comment: D216 (doug-md, 2026-10-17: "three differnt auto runs, 1st one is aggressive, two is passive (avoids combat), 3 is mixed (will fight if provoked)"): how a party walking itself meets bands, picked in the menu and kept in settings.cfg (Pace.auto_style). Aggressive turns aside for any band in sight and walks into its red, and steps into a roadside scene; mixed keeps to its way and fights only what sees it; passive walks round red ground where it can. Inferred: the names and blurbs.

blurbs.aggressive: Walking itself, the company goes looking for a fight: any band in sight, and any trouble on the road.
blurbs.mixed: Walking itself, the company keeps to its way and fights only what comes for it.
blurbs.passive: Walking itself, the company goes round whatever is watching the ground, and leaves trouble on the road to others.

board._comment: D359 (Ewan's play-test 3, item 7: the Guild's board read at the board, not from anywhere in town): a village's, a keep's and Stormreach's work is taken off the notice board standing by the Guild's clerk (a prop with "reads": "board" in the area), walked up to and looked at (E, or a click); J still reads it, standing there. A place with no board on its ground (a hut) is asked as before. bare_line is said at a board with nothing on it for the company.
board.bare_line: Nothing pinned to it is for you today.

vision._comment: D361 (play-test 7, item 11: 'the chapter visions shown as pictures'): a chapter memory picked up plays its lines over a vision. It opens on the line after `opens_after` (the floor going out from under the world), a wash of `wash` with the memory's own picture (A65, art/visions/<memory id>.png) or, until that is drawn, its keepsake held up at `keepsake_height` of the screen, drawing `closer` over `closer_seconds`; the line whose words are `ends_on` turns it white, and the lines after are back on the floor. Fades take `fade_seconds` (none on Auto). Read by src/area/memory_vision.gd. Inferred: the wash, the sizes and the times.

ground_watch._comment: Bands met on the ground (D66, D68). A band stands in the ground of the tile it camps on, and at the edge of any tile its eyes reach. It watches the cells within sight_base + sight_per_reach x its sight (the world's 2), from where it stands; trees, houses and rock block the line, water and every land's liquid do not, and ground that is cover (cover on its terrain in tilesets.json, or named in cover) is never watched. It stands at least keep_away cells further than that from where the party comes in, and patrols a loop of patrol_points stops within patrol_reach cells, a cell every patrol_step_seconds, resting patrol_pause seconds at each, never bringing where the party came in into sight; its red cells move with it. Walking into a watched cell (or being walked into view of) starts the fight there: spotted_seconds of everyone looking, the band rushing charge_share of the way in charge_seconds (both 0 since D204: the fight is on the moment they see you, and they close in fighting), then the fight on a field field_margin cells round everyone, field_smallest to field_largest (no edge drawn and nothing dimmed on the ground, D204), opening on the ground's own view and drawing back over pull_back_seconds. On the land (D76) a band keeps to its own tile and patrols land_patrol_points stops within land_patrol_reach cells; when the continent moves it to the next tile it walks there across the land, a cell every travel_step_seconds.
ground_watch._comment_first_strike: A first strike (D288, D300): standing out of a band's sight with one of its figures within first_strike_reach cells, G (or a click on the band) winds the lead up for first_strike_seconds, turned to it; then the fight opens as an ambush and the lead's blow lands at once (skirmish.json -> first_strike). Seen while winding up, the strike is lost and the fight is an ordinary one.

classic.blurb: Save whenever you like; the game also saves when you set out, when you rest, when you reach a town, at the Guild, when a gate is shut and when a Tower chapter ends. When your lead falls you may reload the last save, or ascend and choose the next lead.

iron_man.blurb: One life. The game saves itself when you set out, when you rest, when you reach a town, at the Guild, when a gate is shut, when a chapter ends, every time you come back to the map, and when you leave. When your lead falls they ascend, and the save goes with them.

gentle.blurb: For the story and for testing. Weakened foes, generous spoils, full recovery after each fight, and nobody dies for good.

first_hour.blurb: Where a new life starts. Foes a little softer and the road a little kinder than Even, but a fall is still the end of that world.

even.blurb: The game as it is written.

hard.blurb: Preparation is the only thing between you and the ground.

breeze.blurb: Friction-free testing mode. Party sweeps through battles with high mobility, 10x XP/gold, and zero permadeath.

tower._comment_walked: D102: floors 1 to walked_floors are walked, each on its own ground (`walked_area`, with the floor number), with bands watching it and the stair up at the far end; the last is kept by a keeper. Above them a floor was fought as one battle on a screen of its own; since D207 it borrows one of their plans (borrowed_plans).
tower._comment_own_bands_from: D254: from this floor up, a floor with ground of its own (6 to 10, the Second Hour) has its bands restocked with the floor's own foes as a borrowed plan's are (tower_floors.gd), all but its keeper, so the Second Hour climbs as D189, D222 and D243 tuned the floors above it.
tower._comment_borrowed_plans: D207: every floor above the walked ones is walked too, on one of their plans in turn (tower_floor_N for N in this list; floor 5's is left out, its keeper being the Warden of the Fifth). Its bands are its own: each of the plan's bands is the floor's foes as a fought floor would have them (level_base, levels_per_floor, meet_the_party, the cohort, foes_min to foes_max), and on the top floor the plan's first band is the Spire Apex's keeper and the rest stand down. Floors 6 to 10 have their own rooms since the Second Hour (D196, D254); floors 11 up borrow 1 to 4.
tower._comment_fought: D189 (play-test 4: floors 6 to 20 were easier than 1 to 5, fights over in three seconds): a fought floor's foes start where floor 5's keeper left off and climb from there, are never below the party's own level (`meet_the_party`), and bring one more for every member past `foes_per_member_past` (`foes_max` at most).
tower._comment_upper_bite: D222 (doug-md's play log, 2026-10-17: floors 6 to 20 won with nobody below a quarter of their health): from `from_floor` up, every foe's attack is multiplied by `base`, climbing `per_floor` a floor, to `most` at most. Read by Encounter.upper_bite; the fight applies it as `bite` on the foe.
tower._comment_themes: D364 (doug-md's play-test 3, item 9: 'Tower floors with themes, an ice floor of ice creatures, goblins in winter coats'): from floor `from`, every floor that does not close a chapter (a keeper's) takes the next theme in `list` in turn, floor 6 the first. A theme's `units` are the floor's foes instead of its cohort's (Encounter.for_tower; tiers still dealt), `tint` its light, `name` added to its title and `line` said as the party comes up onto it. Goblins in winter coats wait on their art. Inferred: the four themes, their creatures, tints and lines.

list.name: the Frost Floor
list.line: Frost on the stone and breath that shows. Whatever lives up here was made for the cold.

list.name: the Drowned Floor
list.line: Water stands in the joints of the floor, and something moves under it.

list.name: the Ember Floor
list.line: The stone is warm underfoot, and ash drifts up the stair from somewhere below.

list.name: the Warren
list.line: Bones and bedding in every corner: a goblin warren, dug into the Tower's own stone.

tower._comment_chapter_ask: D364 (doug-md's play-test 3, item 9: 'perhaps "Are you sure?" before leaving floor 5'): the stair off a floor that closes a chapter asks before it climbs, the first press saying what closing the chapter does and the second within `seconds` climbing; anything of the lead's still lying on the floor is named. Auto, which takes the keepsake first, climbs without asking. {floor}, {chapter}, {left} and {key} are filled in. Read by area_scene._sure_of_the_stair. Inferred: the words and the time.

chapter_ask.line: The stair off floor {floor} closes chapter {chapter}. Time passes below, the gates that were brewing open, and the stair above stays shut until the company has answered the world. {left}{key} again to climb.
chapter_ask.keepsake_left: Something of yours still lies on this floor.

tower._comment_cohorts: D243: each stretch of floors fields its factions in turn, a floor each. Up to 15 the Ember Wilds and the Wild; the Ooze stood there until 2026-10-17, so every odd floor from 7 to 15 was slimes, which a beginner practises on and a party of level 8 to 10 never felt (doug-md's play log: floors 11 to 15 easier than 1 to 5).
tower._comment_grown: D290, D307 (meeting six, piece F): every floor from grown.from up is laid out at the climb (TowerFloors.ensure_grown, registered as `area` with the floor number) rather than borrowing floors 1 to 4's plans: a run of chambers from the way in at the bottom to the stair at the top, in the Tower's own stone, the higher the bigger (width and height grow width_per_floor and height_per_floor a floor over floor 10, to widest and tallest; chambers grow one every chambers_every floors, to most_chambers), and a band of the floor's own in every chamber but the first (band_pack is a stand-in the floor's foes replace, TowerFloors.restock). A shared floor (shared_from, then every shared_every) has another company climbing it: shared_size of life.climbers.units at the party's level, named from life.climbers.companies, who fight every fight on the floor beside the party (shared_line). From living_from, every living_every floors people have set up by the stair and live there (living_size of them, living_line, living_talk). Inferred: every number, which floors are shared, where the first living floor is.

grown.hint: WASD to walk  ·  the stair up is north, at the far end  ·  bands hold the chambers
grown.shared_line: Another company is on this floor: {company}. They are going up too, and they fight beside you.
grown.living_line: People live on this floor. {company} set up by the stair long ago, and they are not going higher.

hello: Welcome to the floor. We don't climb any more; we keep it.
You're going up? Then you'll want to rest first. Everyone does, here.

ask.a: Twenty years, some of us. Nobody ages in here, so nobody has to leave. The stair above is for the young.
More floors, bigger each time. Companies go up past us every season. Fewer come down.

living_talk._comment_pool: Play-test 8, ask 2 ('a lot more dialogue options for characters that you meet in the towers'; call BX): each of the floor's folk past the host and the trader is also asked pool_shown of the pool, drawn by src/chronicle/company_talk.gd the same way every time for the same one. Inferred: every line.

pool.a: I got as high as I wanted to be. The stair kept going. I didn't.
Once, to the door. The light outside hurt my eyes. I came back up the same day.

pool.q: What do you eat up here?
pool.a: What comes up the stair on somebody's back, and what grows under the lamps. Not much grows. Enough does.
A few a season. Most rest a night and go on. There's a mark on the wall for every one that comes back down past us.

pool.q: How many marks are on the wall?
pool.a: Count them if you like. It won't take you long.

pool.q: Are there more floors like this?
pool.a: Every few floors somebody has settled. We trade between them when anyone is going that way.
Safer than the floor below. Nothing comes down the stair while folk live by it. We don't ask it why, in case it stops.
No. People who say they have usually want something from you.

living_talk.bye: Mind the stair. We'll be here when you come down, if you do.

grown._comment_living_offers: D317 (D290: 'by floor 25 or 30 people have set up base and live there'): what a living floor offers. The first of its people is the host, who rests the whole company for living_host.heal.price (Talk's mend of everyone hurt, nothing when nobody is), the second the trader, who sells living_trader.sells at the Market's price times living_trader.markup, restocked; the rest talk as living_talk. Inferred: the price, the wares and the mark-up.

living_host.name: the one who keeps the floor
hello: You'll want to rest before the stair. Everyone does, here; it is what we are for.
Sit. Nothing comes down the stair that we have not seen before.

ask.a: The beds, the fire and the stair. Nobody here has grown a day older since they came, so nobody has had to give the work up.

ask.q: How long have you kept this floor?
ask.a: Since before the stair above was found. Long enough that I stopped asking how long.
Others like us, here and there. Some are kinder than me. Some charge more.

heal.done: There. Sleep came easier than you thought it would. Go up when you are ready.
heal.whole: You are whole already. Rest anyway, if you like; it costs nothing to sit.

living_host.bye: Go up rested. We will keep the fire in for you.

living_trader.name: the one who sells
hello: Everything up here came up the stair on somebody's back. The price says so.
Bread, herbs, a draught. Nobody carries more than that this high.

ask.a: Climbers, mostly, paid in what they'd sooner not carry back down. Bread for a sword, once. You'd be surprised.
Not up here. Sell what you find at the bottom, where somebody needs it.

living_trader.shop: What came up the stair. Coin first, mind.
living_trader.sold: Carried up for you, in a way.
living_trader.bye: Climb well. Come back down with something to sell me.

opened: A seat opens at the fire.
Word of floor {floor} has gone down the Tower ahead of you. Sellswords who would not have looked at you stand you drinks now.
{lead} can lead {seats_word} into a fight from today.
party.next_seat: Hire someone in a village or keep to fill it. Floor {next_floor} of the Tower opens one more.
party.all_seats: Hire someone in a village or keep to fill it. Six is as many as anyone has ever kept alive in there.
party.full: Every seat is taken ({seats} of {seats}). Clear floor {next_floor} of the Tower and another opens.

gate._comment_pitch: How hard a gate's bands stand against the party (D273), one value a rank from E to S: a band stands at the party's level or the gate's rank level (Site.expected_level), whichever is higher, plus level, plus per_floor for every floor down (rounded down). E, D and C keep what they had (0, and a whole level a floor). Before D273 every rank had that, and the gate clock's party of four at a B, A or S gate's own level lost its lead in most runs. Inferred: every number.
gate._comment_inside: D248 (doug-md, play-test 6: "When I enter.or get close to a gate, I want to be able to enter into the gate and fight the monsters there and create a whole area where I can fight the monsters in it. I don't want to have to fight the monsters outside the gate."): going into a gate opens its inside, one floor at a time, walked like the Tower's floors (src/chronicle/gate_inside.gd). Each floor is a run of chambers from the doorway at the bottom to the way down at the top, width + width_per_rank x the rank's place (E 0 to S 5) wide and height + height_per_rank high, with chambers + chambers_per_rank of them; a band of the gate's own holds every chamber but the first, and on the last floor the keeper holds the last, before the way down, which does not open until it falls. The ground and walls are the gate's own look (themes, by the gate's place, with the ground sheets drawn bottom first; default for any other); band_reach is how far a chamber's band sees. Walking back out of the doorway leaves the gate. Inferred: every number and every look.

inside._comment_length: Gates that grow (D261): the longer the rank the longer the gate: floors_per_rank (with floors_base, Site.floors) and chambers_per_rank make an E gate one floor of three chambers and an S gate five floors of seven; a chamber of rank from_rank_two_bands or above holds two bands when it rolls under two_band_chance. The keeper is keeper_stout times as hard to put down at each rank (E to S), so an S keeper's fight runs minutes, not seconds. On every floor but the last the way down opens only once every band on it is down (rout); on the last, the keeper's fall scatters whatever is left (scatter_line). Inferred: every number.
inside.rout_line: The way down will not open while anything on this floor still stands.
inside.scatter_line: With its keeper down, everything else in the gate breaks and scatters into the dark.
inside._comment_grounds: Gates that grow (play-test 7, D261): a gate's inside is ground of its own kind. The first floor is the kind of the land the gate stands on (by_land, by Biome id; by_area first, for a gate whose mouth has a look of its own); deeper floors of a gate of rank from_rank_vary or above take another kind each, rolled from the gate and floor. A kind with `biome` takes that land's floor, bare ground (the path), pool (the walls, unless `wall` says) and cover, and its sheets; `open` widens its chambers by two cells a step and its passages by two, so a plain is open ground and a cave is tight. Inferred: every kind, its look and which land gives which.
inside.hint: Bands hold the chambers. The way down is at the far end; the doorway behind you is the way out.

gate._comment_walk_in: D354 (play-test 7, item 11: 'walking into a gate or the grove, not cut to it'): gone into from the ground by a player (not Auto), the company walks into the gate's doorway over `seconds`, fading as the screen goes dark, and the floor inside comes up out of the dark over the same. 0 cuts straight in. Read by area_scene._walk_into_the_gate. Inferred: the time.
gate._comment_shut: Gates that grow (play-test 7, D261: "when you defeat a gate or shut a gate, then it should turn off and break apart and be lying on the floor. And I think it would be good to hear cheers from the people around the gates"): a shut gate's mouth shows `art` (drawn in house by tools/draw_broken_gate.py until A38) where the gate stood, and `people` come to look at it, cheering and promising to tell it on (the deed is carried by the world remembers, D249). `cheer` is said as the party comes out of the gate it shut. Inferred: who, where and every line.

shut.cheer: Folk who were keeping well back from the gate come running as it falls, cheering, and the tale is going round before you are clear of it.

people.name: a woman from the hamlet
chatter: You shut it! It has been howling at us since the spring.
My boy will want to hear this from you, not from me. He won't believe me.
Is it done? Truly done? Somebody pinch me.

people.name: an old carter
chatter: Look at it. Lying there like any old stones.
I've carted past that thing every week for a year. Thank you.
Your name'll be in every taproom from here to the city by the week's end.

people.name: a trader passing
chatter: I'll be telling this one on the road for a year.
Drinks are on me the next time we're under the same roof.

gate._comment_reading: D293, D302: a gate's rank is a reading. From rank wrong_from (C) up, one gate in wrong_one_in reads a rank lower than it is, until the company goes in (misread_line). A double gate (double_base in a hundred, and double_per_fallen more for every world already ended, decided the first time it is gone into) climbs a rank the first time it is entered (double_line), and its way out stays shut (sealed_line) until its keeper falls or the company is thrown out. Both are fixed by where the gate stands. **Inferred**: every number and line.

reading.misread_line: {gate} read {read}-rank from outside. Inside, it is {rank}.
reading.double_line: The air thickens as you go in. {gate} was a double gate: its rank climbs from {was} to {rank}, and the way out shuts behind you.
reading.sealed_line: The way out is shut. A double gate lets nobody out until its keeper falls.

gate._comment_fallen: D293, D304 (meeting six, piece D2): in a world after a lead has fallen, some gates hold a demon king, a fallen lead come through wearing their face. From rank from (C) up, base in a hundred, and per_fallen more for every world already ended (the record of the fallen, echoes.past), decided by where the gate stands and kept once seen (data.demon); which of the fallen, by the same hash. Its keeper is the fallen lead's own unit, at the floor's keeper level plus levels and never under the level they fell at, stout_times as hard to put down as the rank's keeper; every band in the gate stands band_levels higher (the hostile forces that came through with them). Going in says line; the map label and the keeper's title carry label and title; the shut gate says shut_line. Words: {name}, {demon}, {gate}, {they}, {their}, {them} and the same capitalised. **Inferred**: every number and line.

fallen.label: Demon King {name}
fallen.line: Something of a burned world holds {gate}, and no reading saw it from outside: {demon}.
fallen.title: {demon} keeps the far side of {gate}. {Their} world burned, and what came through wears {their} face.
fallen.shut_line: {demon} is put down. What came through with {them} goes back to ash, and {their} world stays burned.

gate._comment_instant: D293, D304 (meeting six, piece D2): the Gate Key (key, in GameState.keys) tears an instant gate where it is turned. It is found when the company shuts a gate: always a double gate's (from_double), else one gate in found_one_in of rank found_from or above, fixed by where the gate stands, and never while one is held; the key keeps the rank of the gate it came out of. E on open ground with the key in hand (prompt, {rank}) tears a gate of that rank there, or on the nearest open cell within two when a place stands here: open from that step, held by a faction seated at gates, named names in turn, walked and shut like any other; spent says whether the key is used up. lines: found_line and torn_line ({gate}, {rank}). **Inferred**: every number and line.

instant.found_line: Among what the keeper kept, a key with no lock, warm to the hand: the Gate Key. Turned on open ground it tears a {rank}-rank gate where you stand.
instant.torn_line: The key turns in nothing, and the ground opens: {gate}, a {rank}-rank gate where there was none. Whatever is in it will come out.
instant.prompt: to turn the Gate Key here (a {rank}-rank gate opens where you stand)

rout.brief: Put down everything that comes at you.

guardian.brief: The thing keeping the far side has to fall. What follows it scatters when it does.

heart.brief: Get one of yours onto the gate's heart and the floor gives way to the next.

_comment_hunger: D331 (call BX; Ewan's play-test 8: 'a hunger bar underneath every player so we know how much food they have currently in them and when they need to eat', and Auto eating when needed). Read by src/chronicle/hunger.gd. Everyone in the company is fed 1 (full) to 0, going down per_step with each step on the land (steps_per_day is 8: hungry after about three days, empty after five). Under hungry_below they are hungry: the bar under their health goes amber and hungry_line is said once. At nothing they lose starving_hurt of their health a step, never the last point. Food (taken: eat) fills feeds_per_mend for every point it mends (bread 0.42, a meat pie 0.6) and can be eaten whole when hungry; a bed is a full meal. With Auto on, anyone under auto_eat_below eats the least food that does. Inferred: every number and line.

hunger._comment_tower_floor: D400 (found by bot play, 2026-10-22): the world's steps a Tower floor adds (World.UPKEEP_INTERVAL, 30) do not empty the company (Hunger.pass_over), unless tower_floor_counts. Before, a floor ate 0.75 of a full belly and, once empty, 90% of everyone's health in one lump, so a lead won floor 1 near whole and walked onto floor 2 at 1 HP. Inferred: that the Tower's time is not the company's.
hunger._comment_auto_rests_hungry: D401 (found by bot play, 2026-10-23): a party walking itself makes for the nearest bed (a meal) when anyone is hungry and the packs hold no food. Before, Auto never bought food, a company of four kept walking while one of them starved to 1 HP (the company's whole stayed over auto_rest_below) and the lead fell to the next blow. Inferred: resting, not buying bread.

_comment_nemesis: D330 (call BX; Ewan's play-test 8, after Shadow of Mordor's nemesis system: 'Characters will remember that, and people might hold a grudge'). Out of the First Hour's cut list. A band broken leaves one survivor on survive_chance (never a non_sentient kind), named with an epithet; a band met on the road is led by one on return_chance, level_per_return levels up for each time they have come back, saying the confront_lines (the first, then the second...); beaten again they are finished (finished_line, a deed). thanks: a settled errand's giver remembers it on chance, and a traveller on the road's clock is one of them on meet_share, giving gift_share of the errand's pay. Inferred: every number and line.

nemesis.escaped_line: One of them crawls off into the brush clutching a wound. {name} will not forget this.
nemesis.finished_line: {name} will not crawl away this time.
confront_lines: {name} draws steel with shaking hands: "I lived through your blades at {place}. I swore I would never run twice."
{name} again, harder for it: "{place} first, and then the road. Third time I finish it."
{name}, who has stopped counting: "You keep leaving me alive. That was your mistake."

lines: {giver} is coming the other way, and stops when they see who it is.
"You saw to {title} for us. Nobody else would have. Take this, it's not much." ({gift})

_comment_quick_wheel: D326 (call BX; Ewan's play-test 8, after Ark Survival Evolved: hold the scroll wheel for a quick menu). Holding the middle button still for `hold` seconds opens a ring round the pointer; point and let go to take one, let go in the middle for nothing. `walking` is the ring on the land, `fighting` while a fight is on (eat: the picked fighter takes the least food that mends them; stance: the picked fighters' next stance). Inferred: what the ring holds and the hold time.

mouse_bar._comment: The mouse bar on a computer (D390): every key the walk answers as a button down the right edge, under the corner map, each hover naming its key. `action` is pressed as that input action and its key (as rebound) is named on the hover; `signal` asks for a screen on EventBus instead (`party`, `journal`, `map`, `wheel`, `menu`), and `key` names a bare key. It steps aside in a fight on the ground, which has its own column (D391).

touch_words._comment: What the lines say on a phone (D377): a keyboard's keys said as the touch bar's buttons. `names` is what the touch bar calls an action; `walk` says the stick; `swaps` are [regex, replacement] pairs run in order over any line written for a keyboard (hints, footers, a tip without its own `touch` words) while the touch controls are on and no pad is in hand.

Right-click a place: Go here, or Place a marker
