screen_layout._comment: D351 (Ewan's play-test 8: 'when in-game I'm able to edit the size of them and choose where I want to place them on my screen'): src/ui/screen_layout.gd. From the menu's Arrange the Screen, or Arrange on the quick wheel, a frame is drawn round each panel of the walked ground's screen: dragged to move it; a panel with resize 'size' has a handle at its corner to make its box bigger or smaller; the wheel over any frame grows or shrinks it and its words, between least_scale and most_scale by scale_step. 'words' is the box people talk in. Kept in user://settings.cfg [layout] as a share of the screen; keep_showing pixels of a panel always stay on it.
screen_layout.bar: Drag a panel to move it, its corner to size it, the wheel over it to grow its words.

dispatch._comment_gates: D278 (Ewan's play-test 7: 'send your own characters to do quests so they go on auto mode ... into a dungeon gate'): a band of the company's own people sent to a known gate walks there on the clock, spends steps_per_floor a floor inside, and shuts it on gate_win_base + gate_per_level x (the band's average level - the gate's expected level) + gate_per_hand for every member past the first, kept between gate_min and gate_max. Sending anyone away opens once the company has shut a gate of its own.
dispatch._comment_wilds: D348 (the rest of Ewan's 'send your own characters to do quests so they go on auto mode'; D309, D310): a band sent to a wild place the company has heard of, whose guard still stands, walks there on the clock, spends steps_in_wild steps inside, and drives the guard off on wild_win_base + gate_per_level x (the band's average level - the guard's, which is the company's level when the first set off) + gate_per_hand for every member past the first, kept between gate_min and gate_max. Won: the guard is beaten for the run, the chests come home in the packs, and a job to clear it is done. Lost: each rolls for their life. **Inferred** (agenda 256).
dispatch._comment_meet: D294, D300 (founders' meeting: 'clear that rank E gate and meet me back at Stormreach'; if you are not there, a crow brings word): sent with a village, keep or the house to meet in, they walk there from where the job was done, a tile a step. With the company there they fall in; if not, crow_line is said and they wait there until it comes. With none named they come back to wherever the company is, as before.
dispatch.crow_line: A crow finds the company: {names} {are} back at {place}, and {wait} there for you.
dispatch._comment_auto: D349 (BR9's 'sending your own people out on Auto'; D294: 'run on Auto by their moods and nature'): somebody sent on Auto picks their own work from what the company knows within auto.reach tiles (an errand taken, a gate, a wild place), goes, and when they fall in again takes the next, until called back or hurt below auto.rest_below of their health. Each job is weighed by its odds (an errand at errand_odds) plus boldness x what it is worth (worth); a job below least_odds - boldness x bold_floor is never taken. Boldness is bold_base, plus bold_letters for each letter of their temper, plus bold_per_mood for every point their mood stands above the base (less below it), kept between 0 and 1. **Inferred** (agenda 257): every number.

auto.idle_line: {name} is on Auto, but there is nothing within reach worth the risk. They stay with the company until there is.
auto.hurt_line: {name} comes back hurt, and comes off Auto to mend.

experience._comment_gates: D301 (the founders' meeting of 2026-10-20): with levels_only_in_gates, the first of a kind teaches only when it falls inside a gate or a cave (a fight whose encounter says `teaches`); on the land and in the Tower it is only noted in the log of foes (character.met), and practice (proficiency) is what grows there.

recruit._comment_wares_on_show: D146 (the designers' fortnight, F4): how many of a place's wares are laid out at once; Z turns to the next and B buys the one in hand.

_comment_sellswords: D295 (meeting six: mercenaries hired for gold who stay until the job is done; built as the Gilded Flagon's book, src/chronicle/sellswords.gd): `board_size` sellswords offered at once, dealt again every `refresh_steps` world steps; each one of `templates` at the lead's level give or take one, for one of `jobs` (gate: until the next gate is shut; chapter: until the next chapter of the Tower closes), at cost_base + cost_per_level a level, times the job's `price`, the difficulty's prices and the lead's haggling. They bond with nobody and are not among the 32 (D303). Inferred: every number, name and line.

gate.for: until the next gate is shut

chapter.for: until the next chapter of the Tower closes

lines.hired: {name} takes the coin, counts it twice, and falls in.
lines.done: {name}'s job is done. They take their pay and go their own way.
lines.none: Nobody on the book today. Come back in a while.

_comment_heights: D287, D308 (meeting six, piece C2, the first ground with heights): a terrain in tilesets.json with `height` stands that many heights up; a step down is free, a step up one height only onto or off a cell in the area's `ways_up` (a slope drawn there), two or more never (AreaMap.may_step). A drop of hurt_from heights or more hurts everyone walking: share of their health for each height past the first, never below floor of it (hurt_line, {fell}); dropping one says nothing. Trying to climb a shelf with no way up says blocked_line once a cell. Fights, Auto's paths and click-to-walk do not yet know heights; death from the clouds waits for a mountain area. Inferred: every number and line.

land._comment: D332 (after D283, Ewan's play-test 7: 'the world is very flat ... you need to be able to tier it in heights'; and D287's heights on the world map): every generated ground of the land gets rises of its own floor, a height up, climbed only at a slope like the scarp's shelves (D308). `rises` of them on average (a land's biomes.json features.rises wins), plus `on_terrain` more on that world terrain. A rise keeps `margin` cells off the tile's edges so where tiles meet is level, and a cell off every path and water. Each piece of higher ground gets a slope (`slope_art`) on an edge with open ground in front, the south first, and a second from `second_slope_from` cells. The `sheet` (tools/draw_rises.py) draws the rise's face. Laid by their own roll, so nothing else on a ground moves for them (src/area/ground_gen.gd).

heights.blocked_line: The shelf is too high to climb here. Find a slope, or carry a rope.
heights._comment_ladders: D337 (D287: 'walls and heights can be scaled some way'): a ladder (an area's `ladders`, drawn landmark/ladder) is climbed up as far as ladder_most heights; a Climbing Rope carried (rope_item, in the packs or worn by anyone in the company) makes every face one height up a way up, for the lead, the company and Auto alike. Fights keep to slopes and ladders. **Inferred** (agenda 245): two heights a ladder, and the rope.
heights.rope_line: The rope goes over the edge, and up you go.
heights.hurt_line: A drop of {fell}. Everyone lands hard.
heights._comment_paths: D312: on ground with heights every way found (a click, Auto, a band on its rounds, a person at work) steps only where a walker may, so it goes round by a slope rather than at the shelf; a drop that would hurt counts path_drop_cost cells more, so a way round is taken when there is one. A click on a shelf with no way up from here says no_way_line, once a cell.
heights.no_way_line: There is no way up to there from here.
heights._comment_fights: D313: a fight on ground with heights carries them. A fighter steps down anywhere and up one height only at a way up (a slope), as a walker does; a body is never shoved up a ledge, and shoved off one it falls: shoved_off.share of its health for every height fallen, and it lies knocked down for down_seconds, said as word over it and line in the log.
heights._comment_from_above: D343 (the founders at meeting six, D287/D299: 'a blow or a shot from above'): on a fight laid over ground with heights, a fighter standing higher than the one they hit lands `blow` more a height up at arm's length, `shot` more a height for anything reaching further, counted up to most_heights; the log tags it 'From above'. Level ground, a blow upward and a hand-made field (heights there are the jump's) are unchanged. **Inferred** (agenda 251).
heights._comment_on_the_map: D343 (D287: heights on the world map): the map of the continent draws each cell per_height lighter for every height of its terrain (hill 1, crag 2) and lit from the north-west, slope lighter a height the ground climbs towards the south-east (darker where it falls), held to most either way; from peaks_from_px pixels a cell, a hill carries one small peak and a crag two (peaks_most). **Inferred** (agenda 251).

shoved_off.line: {who} is knocked off the edge, a drop of {fell}.

heights._comment_clouds: D321: a mountain's top has the clouds below it (terrain `clouds` in tilesets.json). Walking, nobody steps off into them, and the lead says cloud_line once a cell. In a fight a body shoved into a cloud cell goes over and is gone: a foe dies there, credited to whoever shoved it; one of the company falls at once, with no friend near enough to pull them back, no hearth and nobody to take them, so only a charm, lore or luck saves them (and on a gentler setting they are pulled clear, out of the fight).
heights.cloud_line: Below the edge there is only cloud, white and slow and a very long way down.

into_clouds.line: {who} goes over the edge into the cloud, and is gone.

_comment_wilds: D287, D309 (meeting six, piece C3): places worth going to. The wilds are sites of kind `wild` on the map (tools/place_wilds.py puts per_world of them on their own kind of ground), unknown until the party walks onto one or hears of it. At rest in a village or a keep, on rumour_chance, the host speaks of the nearest wild not yet known within rumour_within tiles (rumour_line: {host}, {wild}, {way}, {days} at steps_per_day a day, {lure} from the area's own `lure`), which marks it on the map. Walking into one for the first time says found_line and writes it in the annals. Inferred: every number and line.

wilds._comment_walk_in: D360 (play-test 7, item 11: 'walking into a gate or the grove, not cut to it'): from the ground the company walks into the nearest trees within reach cells (or ahead cells the way the lead faces) over seconds, fading as the screen goes dark, and the grove comes up out of the same dark. Auto goes straight in. Inferred: the time, the reach.
wilds.rumour_line: {host} speaks of {wild}, {way} of here, {days} off: {lure}. It is marked on your map.
wilds.found_line: {wild}. Few come this way; the ones who did left things behind.
wilds._comment_guard: Creatures that match the land (D287): a band of the land's own foes (biomes.json `foes`, the great beasts held back by `foe_levels`, else the faction that walks the ground) stands by the chest farthest from the way in, `guard_size` of them at the party's level, seeing `guard_reach` cells; beaten, it stays beaten for the run (its done flag).
wilds._comment_story: D314 (D287: 'a quest or a story in each'): every wild tells a story in three pages, spots with `page` in the area, each said once a run when stood on and kept as a flag (story:<area>:<x>:<y>); the last page read says the area's `story.end` and writes story_annals in the annals (story:<area>:told).

herbs_on_land._comment: D335 (D299: 'herbs on the land'; Ewan's play-test 7: 'combine herbs together to make potions'): about per_tile patches a tile of open land, each one of what its land grows (by_land, a land not named grows none), off the paths and the water, picked once a run into the packs (a prop with an item, src/area/ground_gen.gd _herbs). herbs gives each its art, name and lines. **Inferred** (agenda 243): which lands grow what, and how many.

herbs.name: bitter herbs
herbs.line: Bitter herbs, the kind a draught wants. You pick a handful.

redcap.name: redcaps
redcap.line: Redcaps in the damp, bright as a warning. You cut the best of them.

frostmoss.name: frostmoss
frostmoss.line: Frostmoss, pale and cold to the touch. You peel a strip off the stone.

makings_on_land._comment: D346 (the settled BR list, 2026-10-19: crafting; D280's 'forging a new weapon from parts is later'): what a smith forges with, found on the open land like the herbs (D335) and by a roll of their own, so the herbs stand where they stood: about per_tile a tile of a land that has any (by_land), picked once a run into the packs. looks gives each its art (art_wanted, A62, drawn in its place once made), name and line. **Inferred** (agenda 254): which lands have what, and how many.

ash_stave.name: a fallen ash bough
ash_stave.line: A fallen ash bough, straight and seasoned. You trim a stave from it.

iron_ore.name: a seam of iron
iron_ore.line: Rust-red stone where the ground has split. You knock out what ore you can carry.

caravans._comment: D334 (D287: 'places worth going to (... hamlets, caravans)'): a caravan is a wild place that walks. Each upkeep it rolls up to tiles_per_upkeep tiles on towards the next town of its route, by the way a party would walk (looked for no further than longest tiles), never onto ground within clear_of_sites of another place nor within party_clear of the party, and never while the party is that close. Within stand_off of the town it stands for rest_upkeeps upkeeps, then sets off for the next. src/chronicle/caravans.gd. **Inferred** (agenda 242): the pace and the rests.

caves._comment: D282 (Ewan's play-test 7: 'a cave system, so like in pokémon. You can go into a cave and it'll be a whole different area'). A walkable tile of one of `terrains` has a cave mouth on `chance`, the same tiles every time for a world (src/chronicle/caves.gd). Inside it is laid out as one gate floor of a rank from `ranks` (by the same roll), in the gate's cave ground, with no way further down; its bands are held, its deepest the strongest, and a cache beside that one holds `gold_low`-`gold_high` copper and one of `finds`. Lost, the party is back outside the mouth (`lost`).
caves.name: the cave
caves.hint: WASD to walk  ·  the way out is the way you came
caves.lost: You crawl back out into the light, and they are still down there.

crafting._comment: D280 (Ewan's play-test 7: 'combine herbs together to make potions, upgrade weapons ... you can buy weapons or you can make them in the blacksmith'). mix: recipes the party screen offers from the packs, anywhere (src/chronicle/crafting.gd). A smith with a talk block's `hone` puts a notch on a weapon somebody carries: +1 attack a notch for that person with that weapon, up to hone_most; a notch costs (hone_base + the weapon's price x hone_share) x the notch, through the difficulty's price dial.
crafting._comment_where: D346: a recipe with at 'hearth' is mixed from the party screen only within hearth_reach cells of a fire (a camp's, a caravan's, the climbers' on a floor) or anywhere in an area that says hearth: true (an inn, a tavern): a fire draws more out of the herbs. One with at 'smithy' is forged by a smith whose talk has `forge`, for its fee (through the price dial), out of what the company gathered on the land (makings_on_land) and carries; a rune's or a recipe's makings carried as a charm count, and are spent. **Inferred** (agenda 254): every recipe and fee.
crafting.brewed_line: Steeped over the fire, slow, nothing wasted: a {made}.
crafting.forged_line: Hammered, quenched and handed over: a {made}. It goes in the packs.
crafting.forge_short_line: The makings are not all there any more.
crafting._enchant: D327, D299 item 3 (the founders: 'enchantments and other stuff you can put on your weapons'). A rune laid on the weapon somebody carries, from the packs, anywhere the party screen opens: its effect is one of the fight's passives (data/skirmish.json), theirs while they carry that weapon, over and above max_passives. One rune a weapon; a new one takes the old one's place.

enchant.description: heals for 10% of the damage dealt
anyone striking from close takes 15% of the blow back
a basic attack has a 10% chance to strike twice

moods._comment: D279 (Ewan's play-test 7: 'a system where characters have emotions ... use inspiration from RimWorld ... so that the characters feel more life-like'; 'some characters won't want to join you in the pursuit of climbing the tower'). A mood is base plus every thought carried (src/chronicle/moods.gd). Thoughts are noticed once a step from what changed: a fight won or lost, a gate shut, a floor of the Tower climbed, a friend (a bond of friend_bond or more) dead. by_group sets a thought's worth by temper group (NT, NF, SJ, SP, as the wanderers read them), so the cold-eyed are glad to climb and the rest are not. A band nudges attack and defense; below break_below, now and then (break_chance a step), one of the company sits out break_steps steps. The lead never does.

bands.name: At the end of their rope

thoughts._comment_more: D347 (call BR's moods, built on): a fall seen of someone who was not a friend; a friend gone their own way (let go, or left); a night's rest; a friend marching beside them, renewed while they do; being looked after (the company mended by a healer for coin) and a better edge on their own weapon (honed or enchanted). Hunger joins them when it lands. Inferred: every label and number.

moods.break_line: {name} has had enough, and goes off on their own a while.

recruit_anyone._comment: D277 (Ewan's play-test 7: 'you can ask someone to join you, they might say no ... do quests with them and gain their trust'). Anyone with a talk block can be asked to walk with the company, unless they keep a post (sells, heal, guild), stand in an area in no_areas, are named in stays, or say "recruit": false. The ask is a Charisma check: d20 + half the best talker's charisma (level x per_level + notoriety, + outward for an E temper) against dc, or story_dc for one of the story folk (data/story_npcs.json). A no is not the end: they name a way to earn their trust (their own favour, if they have one, else one of trust), and once the company has done it they come without a roll. Folk with no name of their own ('a settler') take one when they join.

trust.line: Win three fights with that lot behind you, then ask me again.
Do two jobs for folk who need them done. Then we'll talk.
Put a dozen of the things out there in the ground first. I want to see you can.
Bring back something worth the walk. Three hauls, say. Then I'll know you come home.

recruit_anyone.job_trust: Do that favour for me first. Then I'll know what you're worth.
yes: All right. I've stood here long enough.
Give me a moment to fetch my things. Right. Lead on.
I'd been hoping someone would ask.
no: I've a life here. Ask me when you've given me a reason.
recruit_anyone.waiting: You know what I said. Nothing's changed.
trusted: You did it, then. I said I'd come, and I will.
Fair's fair. I'll walk with you.
recruit_anyone.full: There's no room in that company for one more. Make some and ask me again.

siege._comment: DNEW (play-test 3: 'defending a town under siege (Coldrun, with archers on its towers)'; play-test 4: 'when Stormreach is attacked and defended, see the fight there, not be taken somewhere else and put back'). While a town is threatened its besiegers stand outside one of its gates on the land, the very band its defence is fought against (Encounter.siege_band), and its bowmen stand on the towers nearest that gate. Defend it and the company runs to the inside of that gate over run_seconds; the fight is laid there, the besiegers where they stood, and the bowmen fight beside the company from their towers (a rampart: higher by rampart_height, nobody climbs onto it). Saved, the besiegers are gone; lost, they stand there still. Read by src/area/area_scene.gd. Inferred: how many bowmen, how far out the besiegers stand, and the words.
siege.name: a besieger
chatter: Over the wall, the lot of you!
They'll open up when they're hungry.
Burn it. Burn the lot of it.
siege.seen_line: {town} is under siege: they are at its gate.

news._comment: D365 (doug-md's play-test 2 ask, D118: 'news that travels at the speed of people'). Word of a siege, a town fallen, a gate broken, a nemesis abroad or a floor of the Tower climbed walks out from where it happened at renown.steps_per_tile, as a deed's does: the tidings at a hearth are only what has reached that place, and a siege, a fall or a broken gate further off than heard_at_once_tiles (bells and smoke) is told to the company only when the word reaches it, as word_reaches. Read by src/chronicle/news.gd. Inferred: how near is heard at once, and the words.

remembered._comment: D249 (the world remembers, Ewan's #270 keep 6, issue #286). Read by src/chronicle/remembered.gd. Somebody with a talk block (the Watch, an innkeeper, anyone you can ask things) brings up the newest deed whose word has reached their place, once each, before their hello; a townsperson who only chats says it instead of their chatter on aside_chance. kinds holds the lines by deed kind: warm for a deed people were glad of, cold for one they were not; a deed with no kind of its own is said with told when it was written down the way you would say it to the doer's face. {place} is where it happened, {told} what was done, {name} who did it. Where the company's standing is at or below cold_at, anyone with a talk block and no refusal of their own turns it away on cold.chance, and a coin (cold.bribe) or a word wins them round. A faction whose own bands the company has beaten grudge_at times (none of no_grudge) holds a grudge: its bands see grudge_sight cells further and shout one of grudge_shouts on seeing the company. In a later world, somebody at a place within dream_reach tiles of where an earlier lead did something (dream_most of each lead's deeds are kept) tells of it once, as a dream (dreamt). Every number and word is Inferred (agenda row 162).

text: We know what you did. We've nothing for you.
You've a nerve, walking in here after that.
cold.check_q: That wasn't the whole story. Hear me out.
cold.won: ...Fine. Say what you came to say, then.

grudge_shouts: That's them! The ones who cut down ours!
It's the marked one! For our dead!
That's the lot who did for our kin. Take them!
remembered.grudge_line: {faction} have lost {count} bands to you now. They will know you on sight.
dreamt: Odd, you turning up. I dreamt of someone with that mark on them. {name}, they were called. They {told}. Then the dream went dark.
You'll think me soft, but I've dreamt this before. Someone like you, the mark and all. {name}. They {told}, and then they were gone.

warm: You're the one who shut {place}, aren't you? We felt it go quiet.
{place} is shut. That was you. Folk here sleep a bit easier for it.
They say the light at {place} went out with you stood in front of it.
You held {place} when the raid came. Word got here before you did.
{place} would be ash without you. Somebody's cousin was there.

cold: You're the ones who put {place} to the torch.
We heard about {place}. Everyone's heard about {place}.
There's folk here with family in {place}. Mind yourself.

warm: You stood on top of the Tower. I'll be telling my grandchildren I met you.
tower_topped.told: stood on top of the Tower

warm: Word's come here of you. You {told}.
I heard you {told}. Good on you.
cold: I heard you {told}. Poor thing to be known for.
You {told}, they say. People remember that sort of thing.

fallen._comment: D352 (doug-md's play-test 7, item 5: 'bodies that stay after a fight, searched for loot'). A band beaten on the land leaves its fallen where they dropped: on the ground a thing to walk up to and search (name, line; drawn as art, A63's fallen once drawn and the cache's picture until then (D369)), said with ground_line; off the ground searched at once (searched_line). What they carried is a loot roll of richness_per_foe for each of the band, on dice of its own. Read by world_scene._search_the_fallen. Inferred: every number and line.
fallen.name: the fallen
fallen.line: They lie where they fell. Whatever they carried is yours now.
fallen.ground_line: The fallen lie where they dropped. Search them before you go.
fallen._comment_floors: D362 (play-test 7, item 5, the rest): a band beaten on a gate's or the Tower's floor leaves its fallen where it stood, searched the same way (name, line, art, ground_line, richness_per_foe), on top of what the floor pays. Read by area_scene._lay_the_fallen. Inferred: that floors leave them too, and as much as the land's.

cache_art._comment: Play-test 7 (doug-md: "when I click this gold pile ... it is a sword"): how a cache found on the ground is drawn, by what is in it. Looked up by the piece's kind (Gear.kind, or `charm` for a charm), then by its icon's folder (bone_sword has no kind but a blade icon; never for a charm), then `item` for any other piece; `coin` when it holds only coin. Each is a picture under art/props. The weapons and the rest are A37's sword, bow, staff and bundle lying on the ground, which stand as the Tower's shattered sword and a strongbox until they are drawn (props.json stand_ins, D369). Read by Loot.cache_art.

scars._comment: D218 (from Kenshi's toughness, picked by doug-md 2026-10-17): a fighter who goes down in a fight the company wins, and lives, gains max_hp health for good, up to most scars. line is said at the fight's end ({name}, {hp}, {scars}).
scars.line: {name} will carry a scar from that, and be harder to put down: +{hp} health for good.

keepers._comment: D219 (from Necesse's bosses, picked by doug-md 2026-10-17): every faction's gate keeper carries a prize (an equipment id). The chance it gives it up rises with each keeper of that faction felled since the last prize: chance[0] the first, chance[1] the second, then certain; after a prize it starts again. lines: prize (it drops), missed (it had lost it), with {keeper} and {prize}.

lines.prize: {keeper} falls, and what it guarded falls with it: {prize}.
lines.missed: Every {keeper} carries {prize}. This one had lost it somewhere. The next will not have.

treasure._comment: D220 (from Necesse's map fragments, picked by doug-md 2026-10-17): a band beaten on the land carries a torn treasure-map piece on piece_chance; pieces of them make an X on the map, between near and far steps of walking off (a little of the ground round it charted, chart_radius). Standing on it digs up a find of richness (a cache is about 0.5 to 1.5) that always holds something to carry. One X at a time. lines: piece ({held}, {need}), whole ({need}, {bearing}, {region}), dug, and the quest list's label and detail ({region}).

lines.piece: One of them was carrying a scrap of map, torn from something bigger: {held} of {need}.
lines.whole: The {need} scraps fit. An X, {bearing}, out in {region}. Somebody buried something and never came back for it.
lines.dug: This is where the X was. The ground has been turned before, a long time ago. Something is still down there.
lines.label: The X on your map
lines.detail: Three torn scraps made a map: an X out in {region}, where somebody buried something.

play_hud._comment: D244 (doug-md, 2026-10-17: a small UI for the main screen while playing): the panel under the compass on the ground (top pixels down; top_narrow on a screen narrower than narrow_below, under the top row of buttons), one row a member of the company (face, name, level, a health bar) and the purse. face: the face's size in pixels; bar_width: the health bar's; a bar turns amber under hurt_below of full health and red under low_below. purse: its words ({gold}, {draughts}). tooltip: what hovering it says.

alerts._comment: D245 (after RimWorld's alerts): what wants attention, said under the company, most urgent first. hurt_below: the share of health under which someone counts as badly hurt. Each kind has text (on the panel) and detail (on hover); more is said when there are more than most_alerts.

hurt.detail: {hp} of {max} health. Rest at a village, an inn or a keep, or give them something to eat or drink from the packs (P).

no_draughts.text: Nothing in the packs to mend with
no_draughts.detail: No food or draughts to give the hurt. Bread and draughts are sold in towns.

held.detail: {ransom}, or win them back by force. Press to follow the way there.

siege.detail: Get there and help hold it, or it may fall.

path.detail: Press to open the party screen and choose it.

power.detail: Press to open the party screen and take it.

treasure.detail: Three scraps made it. Press to follow it.

play_hud.tooltip: Your company. Press for the party screen (P).

path_help._comment: D237 (doug-md, play-test 4: a question mark on each path's banner that says what it is in more words): the words for SheetParts.class_help. roles: each fits a path whose growth per level is at_least / at_most these, and (has) whose starting moves include a heal or a shot from range; the first most_roles that fit are said. lines: grows ({max_hp}, {attack}, {defense}, {speed}), starts, move ({name}, {text}), themes ({themes}).

roles.say: Built to stand at the front and take the blows.
Hits very hard, but cannot take much in return.
Keeps the others on their feet.

lines.grows: Each level: +{max_hp} health, +{attack} attack, +{defense} guard, +{speed} speed.
lines.themes: Later powers come from {themes}, uncovered as they grow.

atlas._comment_said_within: D238: walking the ground, a place seen is said to come into sight only once the party is within this many tiles of it, about what the screen shows (play-test 3: Coldrun came into sight before it was on screen); on the map, at once.

lines.fragment: Folded in with it, somebody's map: {place}, out in {region}, {bearing}. It is on yours now.
lines.fragment_stale: Folded in with it, an old map. Everything on it you already know.
